Hi Sanjay — thanks for the follow-ups, and apologies for the slight delay. Sending the package requested below and answering the two clarifying points inline. Files are attached.

Answers to clarifying questions:
1) Fulltext indexing / long-term analytics: None of our listed subprocessors perform long-term fulltext indexing of unredacted customer content by default. We use transient indexing for internal cache/latency features, but persistent indexes that include customer content are only created if explicitly enabled by the customer. For MedCore's default configuration we will not enable persistent indexing.

2) Telemetry vendors and unredacted payloads: Redwood sends aggregated telemetry and anonymized metrics to third-party monitoring providers. We do not forward unredacted request/response payloads (containing customer content) to third-party telemetry vendors. Any debug dumps that could contain payloads are gated by an internal approval workflow and redaction is applied when possible.

Package delivered (attachments):
- redwood_subprocessors_list_2025.csv (CSV, 48KB) — columns: name, service, primary-region, stores_customer_data, encryption_in_transit, encryption_at_rest, contact
- SOC2_Type2_Redwood_2024.pdf (PDF, 2.1MB) — Redacted report suitable for vendor sharing; contains auditor letter and control mappings
- delegation_matrix_medcore.xlsx (XLSX, 120KB) — proposed delegation matrix and recommended onshore options for KMS residency

Key confirmations for MedCore: 
- No subprocessors store unencrypted customer data outside the US by default (for MedCore-configured tenants).
- KMS: Customer keys are supported via BYOK model; for MedCore we can provision a US-resident KMS flow and provide key separation documentation (see delegation matrix).
- Escrow: We offer an escrow mechanism for model artifacts and configuration; details included in the delegation_matrix_medcore.xlsx.

If your auditors need a different SOC package (unredacted sections under NDA), we can coordinate an NDA + secure drop. Let me know next steps and whether legal should prepare a standard data processing addendum for execution.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
